items.title: Betting on war is not an option in Australia. Prediction markets could change that
items.description: Kalshi and Polymarket have gone from obscure start-ups to two of the world's biggest prediction markets where users bet on yes-or-no questions spanning politics, pop culture and war.

items.title: How will new unemployment changes affect Centrelink recipients?
items.description: The federal government has proposed changes to Australia's $2 billion employment services system to make them “more responsive, effective and dignified”.

items.title: Inquiry told giving Jewish security groups greater power 'problematic'
items.description: NSW Police Deputy Commissioner David Hudson has given evidence at the Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion.

items.title: Russia looks for new soldiers in Transnistria as war casualty numbers grow
items.description: The Kremlin is trying to recruit more soldiers for its war in Ukraine but an analyst says at the rate of casualties, "Russia cannot replace recruits fast enough to keep the 'meat grinder' fed."

items.title: ABC's Justin Stevens resigns as director of news
items.description: Justin Stevens, the ABC's director of news, has announced his resignation after 19 years with the organisation.

items.title: NASA has revealed its plan to live on the Moon. Here's how it would work
items.description: The US space agency has outlined plans for a sprawling lunar outpost involving rovers, hopping drones and resource-extraction technology as part of a renewed race to the Moon.

items.title: Live: NSW raised concern about cost of monitoring IS-linked women and children
items.description: The boss of home affairs says the NSW government raised concerns about the cost of monitoring ISIS-linked women and children who have recently returned to the country from Syria. Follow live.

items.title: Headline inflation eases to 4.2 per cent in April as fuel prices fall
items.description: Headline inflation decelerated in April, with consumer prices increasing at an annual pace of 4.2 per cent, down from 4.6 per cent in March.

items.title: This 24yo started gambling as a teenager and has now lost 900k
items.description: From footy tips to Taylor Swift bets, teenagers are being lured into gambling. Almost 34 per cent of Australian teenagers gamble and everyone from teachers, experts, to the young people themselves are sounding the alarm.

items.title: Bystanders foil alleged kidnap attempt of woman changing tyre in Sydney
items.description: A 27-year-old woman was changing a tyre when a man allegedly threatened her with a knife and attempted to drag her into an SUV, NSW Police said.

items.title: Health experts 'alert' not 'alarmed' as measles cases rise in Australia
items.description: Authorities keep a close eye on measles outbreaks in Asia, as many cases reported in Australia continue to be returned overseas travellers.

items.title: More than a million worshippers brave searing heat for annual Hajj pilgrimage
items.description: Thousands of Muslim worshippers converge on the rocky hills and plains of Saudi Arabia's Mount Arafat as the annual Islamic pilgrimage, the Hajj, reached its peak.

items.title: Live: Odds of June rate hike close to zero after inflation fall
items.description: Today's inflation announcement reveals rates have eased to below what was expected, suggesting the Reserve Bank may not raise cash rates next month. Follow live.

items.title: Media leaks ahead of Ben Roberts-Smith arrest referred to corruption commission
items.description: News crews were at Sydney Airport as a plane carrying Ben Roberts-Smith landed, and captured images of his arrest from inside the terminal.

items.title: Cuts of meat that will give you more bang for your buck
items.description: If you are looking to trim your household food budget, lower-cost cuts of meat could be a good place to start. Here are some tips on what to look for and how to cook them.

items.title: Why Blak Douglas won't enter the Archibald Prize again
items.description: The acclaimed Dunghutti artist is using his latest exhibition to challenge perceptions of Aboriginal art and the systemic issues creatives face in Australia.

items.title: More or Less quiz: We need you to rank five State of Origin greats
items.description: If you think you know your stuff when it comes to State of Origin, here's your chance to prove it.

items.title: The BHP files reveal a big problem facing the mining giant
items.description: For a company that prides itself on digging out the metals for the world's clean energy future, saying nothing about its own clean energy future is not an option.

items.title: Police search for missing swimmer in WA's South West
items.description: Police say the woman entered the water at Koombana Bay just after 9:20am and has not been seen since

items.title: 'Inadequate' jail sentence for sex worker killer increased after appeal
items.description: Xiaozheng Lin will spend more time in prison for killing two sex workers in 2022, following an appeal by the prosecutor.

items.title: Council buys land for $1, but what's the catch?
items.description: A Midwest city council buys Crown land for $1 to develop more than 100 dwellings to house key workers, but WA's shadow local government minister says it is an example of more responsibility being placed on councils.

items.title: Teaching student charged with online child abuse offences
items.description: A Victorian teaching student, who had recently worked as a childcare centre cook and was a school council president, is facing charges relating to online child abuse material.

items.title: Public told to stay inside as authorities fight Queensland tyre shop blaze
items.description: Emergency services were called to the business on Queens Road in Kingston just after 1pm, with more than a dozen fire department crews on the scene.

items.title: Original track designer steers clear of estimated $100m MotoGP remodel
items.description: Adelaide Street Circuit designer Bob Barnard estimates it could cost more than $100 million to remodel the track for the MotoGP, but the premier says that number has not been mentioned to him.

items.title: Heavy rain on Gus Lamont's family station prompts police to renew search
items.description: Eight months since Gus Lamont was reported missing, police have again returned to search Oak Park Station as part of an ongoing investigations into the four-year-old's disappearance.
